source_section: §1.4 TIME_WINDOW — Duration; §6 rule_reference values; Evaluation order
subject: Flight duration (window_end - window_start) in the TIME_WINDOW gate

rule.quote: Duration | 15–240 minutes, inclusive at both ends. `window_end` strictly after `window_start`. | `TSD-4` §3
rule.variable: duration_minutes = window_end - window_start (both stored and compared in UTC)
rule.utc_quote: `window_start`/`window_end` are stored and compared in UTC.

preconditions_for_isolation.description: Duration is only evaluated when the earlier gates pass and other TIME_WINDOW conditions do not interfere.
preconditions_for_isolation.evaluation_order_quote: Gates run in a fixed order and evaluation stops at the first failure: **`PILOT` → `AIRCRAFT` → `ZONE` → `TIME_WINDOW`**
baseline: PILOT passes: rating covers zone class, certification current at window_start (OH-1 §2.1, §2.3)
AIRCRAFT passes: weight band in zone's permitted_bands
ZONE passes: altitude <= ceiling, operator authorisation level sufficient, zone active
Lead time >= 6 h and window_start <= 60 days ahead
Zone without curfew (DNI-OPN-1 or KHR-OPN-4) so a 240-minute window cannot touch a curfew
No other APPROVED/UNDER_REVIEW request for the same aircraft overlaps the window

equivalence_classes.name: window_end before window_start (negative duration)
equivalence_classes.note: rule_reference for this case is not stated separately; assumed TSD-4 §3 because it is in the same table row — see U-2

equivalence_classes.name: Duration within allowed range
equivalence_classes.expected: Duration check passes; TIME_WINDOW does not fail on TSD-4 §3

equivalence_classes.name: Window crossing midnight UTC (valid length)
equivalence_classes.range: 15 <= duration <= 240 min, window_start and window_end on different UTC dates
equivalence_classes.expected: Duration check passes (duration computed across the date change)
equivalence_classes.representative: 23:00 → 01:00 UTC next day (120 min), zone without curfew
equivalence_classes.quote: `window_start`/`window_end` are stored and compared in UTC.
equivalence_classes.note: Derived class (date-change risk); the spec does not mention it explicitly

state_transitions.reason: The spec defines no state machine for duration. The only ordering it gives is gate evaluation order (PILOT → AIRCRAFT → ZONE → TIME_WINDOW, stop at first failure). Request lifecycle states (DRAFT, UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED, ...) are named in §1.4 'No overlap' and §5 but transitions are not described in this file.

related_ordering_checks.description: Invalid duration + an earlier gate failing (e.g. PILOT certification lapsed) → failing_gate is the earlier gate, not TIME_WINDOW
related_ordering_checks.quote: `failing_gate` in a `422` response always names the *first* gate to fail, never every gate that would fail.

related_ordering_checks.description: Invalid duration + all earlier gates pass → failing_gate TIME_WINDOW, rule_reference TSD-4 §3

unknowns.question: Time granularity: are window_start/window_end second-precision? Is 14 min 59 s (or 240 min 1 s) rejected? The spec states the range only in whole minutes.
unknowns.impact: Sub-minute boundary values (14:59, 240:01) cannot be assigned an expected result.

unknowns.question: Which rule_reference is returned when window_end <= window_start? The 'strictly after' clause is in the Duration row, but §6 lists only 'Duration out of range → TSD-4 §3'. It could also be a schema-level 400/422 before gates run.
unknowns.impact: Expected result for EP-1, EP-2, BV-1, BV-2 is only partially defined (status/gate assumed).

unknowns.question: Order of conditions inside TIME_WINDOW is not specified. If both lead time and duration fail (or duration and curfew/overlap), which rule_reference is returned?
unknowns.impact: Combination cases inside TIME_WINDOW have no defined expected rule_reference; test duration in isolation (see preconditions).

unknowns.question: Is duration re-checked when a request is edited/resubmitted, or only at submission? The file does not say when gates run in the lifecycle.
unknowns.impact: No state-transition cases can be derived for duration.
